requirement:
The bundled languages report each recognized source comment as `Comment` on
the item that owns it under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Each comment in a run has its own span and the run's owner. Consumers interpret
the comment text.
rationale:
The subject has three obligations. Owner placement itself is delegated to the cited `requirements.references.outline_comments`.

1. **Recognized comments are reported as `Comment`.** `bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs` asserts exact `(kind, source text)` lists for Python, Rust block comments, TypeScript, TSX, CSS, YAML, TOML, Markdown and plain text.
   - It covers recognized comments of each syntax: `#`, `//`, `/* */`, `/** */`, `/*! */` and HTML comment blocks.
   - It also covers non-comments that must not be reported: comment-like text in strings, YAML block scalars, inline HTML comments, comments in code fences, unfinished comments, and `.txt` files.

2. **Each comment in a run has its own span.** `rust_attachments_keep_the_owner_kind_and_original_bytes` has a two-line `///` run. It asserts two separate `Comment` attachments with their own text, and that the first span ends at or before the second begins. The TOML case `# first` / `# second` also expects two separate entries.

3. **Each comment in a run has the run's owner.**
   - In the Rust test, both `///` comments land on `mod[m]/fn[f]`, and `records(2)` asserts both there.
   - The trailing `// trailing` comment lands on the same item.
   - The `//!` comment lands on the root item, `records(0)`.
   - The Python case asserts that `def[f]` holds exactly 3 attachments.
   - `class.py` asserts the owner of the decorator span.

The multi-language test does not check owners for TypeScript, CSS, YAML, TOML or Markdown. Comment ownership is the cited requirement's job, and the Rust and Python assertions already cover owner and run behavior. I did not treat this as a gap.

The obligation that consumers interpret comment text places no behavior on the SDK, so it needs no test. The implementation in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#impl[Outline]#2/fn[from_legacy]` pushes each comment as its own `Comment` attachment on its owner. Both tests carry the `{test}` reference to the subject, so there is no marking gap.

text: :::{req} attachments.comments
The bundled languages report each recognized source comment as `Comment` on
the item that owns it under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Each comment in a run has its own span and the run's owner. Consumers interpret
the comment text.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. Habeas MUST retain the
one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each inline role’s opening brace or
fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
